narrative.title: Compacting a Deduplicated Sensor Timeline
narrative.scenario: An edge gateway stores minute-stamped sensor events in a fixed-size RAM slab that is already sorted by timestamp but littered with repeated ticks. Memory is too tight to allocate a second slab, so the repeated ticks must be squeezed out in place. Report how many leading slots now hold distinct timestamps.
narrative.inputFormat: An array nums of n integers, sorted in non-decreasing order.
narrative.outputFormat: An integer k. The first k slots of nums must hold the distinct values in their original order; anything beyond k is ignored.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order

testCases.explanation: After compaction the slab begins [1, 2], so k = 2 distinct timestamps survive.
The distinct values are 0,1,2,3,4 and they are packed into the first five slots.

hintLevels: Level 1: Since the slab is already sorted, equal timestamps are always neighbours, so one writer position plus one reader position is enough.
Level 2: Keep a write index pointing at the last kept value and advance the reader; when the reader sees a value different from the last kept one, place it at the next write slot.
Level 3: The count you return is one more than the final write index, and a slab holding a single value must return 1 rather than 0.
